findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike Intelligence reported a targeted campaign against South Korean financial organizations, active from late September to early October 2026, in which an unattributed actor used ARTEX alongside large language models for intrusion activity. Analysis of attacker-controlled open directories exposed Claude Code session histories and ARTEX configuration files, and the campaign resulted in data exfiltration from several firms. CrowdStrike assessed with moderate confidence the operators were likely China-nexus, based in part on recovered operator artifacts.
findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance

findings.summary_md: Microsoft Threat Intelligence attributed the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise to Storm-0940, a China state-aligned actor active since 2021. In that incident Storm-0940 used ARTEX to accelerate reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse, attempting sign-ins against more than 2,250 tenants at a peak of 2,900 failures per minute, with over 151,000 failed logons observed in the short campaign. The report establishes ARTEX as nation-state intrusion infrastructure weeks before the exposed-secrets reporting.
findings.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise

findings.summary_md: The Hacker News carried early news coverage of CrowdStrike's findings, reporting that ARTEX had been used in data-theft attacks against South Korean financial firms including Shinhan Bank. The coverage dates the malicious activity to late September through early October 2026 and describes ARTEX as an open-source agentic pentesting framework turned to live intrusions. It is the earliest dated general news account of ARTEX-driven intrusions found in this backfill.
findings.title: ARTEX AI Pentesting Tool Used in Data Theft Attacks on South Korean Financial Firms
